newsitem.title: USA: Bradlees has smaller first-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Bradlees has smaller first-quarter loss.

text.p: Bradlees Inc. said Thursday its losses narrowed in the first quarter, aided by lower expenses and fewer markdowns on merchandise.

The discount retailer, which is trying to reorganize in bankruptcy proceedings, reported a net loss of $32 million, or $2.81 a share, for the quarter ended on May 3, compared with a loss of $53.7 million, or $4.71 a share, a year earlier.
Sales fell to $277 million from $350 million, reflecting the closing of 27 stores since last year's first quarter, and a decline of 6.4 percent in sales at stores open at least a year.
Bradlees operates 109 stores in seven Northeastern states.
It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on June 23, 1995. In Chapter 11 a company is protected from its creditors as it tries to work out a plan to pay its debts.
Trading in Bradlees' stock was suspended on May 1 and it has been delisted from the New York Stock Exchange.
